summary_for_children: Al-Kafirun teaches clarity in worship: for you is your religion and for me is mine.
environment_concept: A meadow path divides into two paths that run side by side to the horizon and never cross. Paired standing stones mark the repeated ayahs. No people are shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Forking path with a low wall between its two branches, four pairs of standing stones.

areas.name: The Paired Stones
areas.description: Four pairs of standing stones for the four ayahs that answer each other (109:2-5).

areas.name: Two Paths
areas.description: Two paths that run side by side and never cross.

activities.name: Read the six
activities.description: Put the six ayahs of Al-Kafirun in order. Look closely: ayahs 2 to 5 are alike.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Meaning of Worship
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Kafirun teaches clarity and steadfastness in worship. It reminds us that beliefs should not be changed merely to please others. People can disagree, and we can remain clear about our faith without being unkind.

world_idea.title: The Courtyard of Conviction
world_idea.description: Explore an architectural reflection space and learn to communicate beliefs respectfully through fictional, age-appropriate dialogues.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
